SUCCESSOR TO THE studio-space-priority-desk EPIC. Named by charter D128, by full slug, because it already existed — minting a second one would fork the ledger. Wave 8 (THE RULING) refused the seal (D120) and handed this task the arithmetic rather than the grievance. Everything needed to DECIDE is written below; a cold reader needs no charter to act on it.

THE HEADLINE: AN UNOBSTRUCTED COLUMN IN THE STATE THE USER CHOSE.

Where it fails: at viewport 1024, with the panel open by one deliberate click, the reader gets 38.00ch of a 55ch bar — a 219px collapse (599px -> 378.958px) on one click. spd-b29 RELOCATED the crush from the default state into the state the user chooses; it did not remove it (D108).

=====================================================================
1. THE MEASURED USER-OPENED TABLE (charter D127) — all seven sub-wide widths
=====================================================================

Source: scripts/studio-desk-measure.mjs run against DEPLOYED guerrilla, and — for the first time in this epic — COMMITTED, at scripts/measurements/spd-visible-table-2026-07-20.json (landed on origin/main in c30d4a2d2, "the instrument stops failing silently and writes its artifact"). Every figure below is TRANSCRIBED from that file. Nothing here is derived, and nothing here depends on prose in a closed task.

=====================================================================
1a. THE VERDICT FIELD, AND THE FIFTEEN-CELL TRAP (wave-9 D139)
=====================================================================

READ THIS BEFORE QUOTING ANY NUMBER ABOVE.

Every row carries TWO verdict booleans and on the twenty-one desktop user-opened cells THEY DISAGREE BY
FIFTEEN:

    content_meets_55ch  =  20 of 21 MEET      <-- the LAYOUT box. NOT the verdict field.
    visible_meets_55ch  =   5 of 21 MEET      <-- what the reader can actually SEE. THE VERDICT FIELD.

visible_meets_55ch IS THE VERDICT FIELD. content_meets_55ch IS NOT. A successor that quotes the layout
field would report 20-of-21 MEET in the exact state this task exists to fix, and would close on a number
produced by measuring a box the inspector is sitting on top of. The whole reason the occlusion-derived
metric was built (D109/D112) is that at viewport 1024 the two move in OPPOSITE directions on one click.

THE ARITHMETIC, on D107's seven fixed desktop widths (1440, 1280, 1024, 900, 800, 764, 700) x three faces
= 21 cells, user-opened state, visible field:

    5 MEET / 16 FAIL.

    The five MEETs are all at the two WIDE widths: 1440 x three faces, plus 1280 native and
    1280 Source Serif 4. 1280 Georgia FAILS at 53.95ch.

    THE CLEAN SUB-WIDE CLAIM: at 1024, 900, 800, 764 and 700, across all three faces —
    15 of 15 FAIL. Not one width, not one face.

DECOMPOSITION — 13 OVERLAY-CAUSED, 3 INHERITED. Charging all 16 to the inspector DOUBLE-COUNTS the
default shortfall, so the split is stated rather than the total:

  - 13 OVERLAY-CAUSED: the cell MEETS in the default state and FAILS after one deliberate click.
    These 13 are the inspector's own cost and are the successor's actual subject.
  - 3 INHERITED: the cell FAILS in BOTH states, so the inspector did not cause it. All three are
    FORCED GEORGIA, at viewport 1280 (53.95ch default), 1024 (54.22ch default) and 700 (51.33ch
    default). These belong to the DEFAULT-state shortfall and their owner is
    spd-b42-georgia-default-shortfall-inflow-width — NOT this task, and not the inspector.

THE MECHANISM behind the five MEETs — the inspector is a different component above and below 1280:

    1440 and 1280:  position STATIC, width 300px, z-index auto, overlays_surface FALSE,
                    overlap_over_surface_px 0, overlap_over_content_box_px 0, scrim renders FALSE,
                    one-click delta 0.000px. THE INSPECTOR DOCKS. Opening it costs the reader NOTHING.
    1024 and below: position ABSOLUTE, width 300px, z-index 5, overlays_surface TRUE,
                    overlap_over_content_box_px 192-276 (192 at 900, 242 at 800, 260 at 1024,
                    276 at 764 and 700), scrim renders TRUE at alpha 0.55. IT OVERLAYS.

That is the whole story of the 5/16 split: where the inspector docks the bar survives, where it overlays
the bar dies. Docking is not, however, an available fix at 1024 — see section 2, where it is arithmetically
dead.

THE SHARPEST CELL, quoted because it is the one a reader feels:
    viewport 1024, native (Iowan Old Style, 18px, probe 10.0000 px/ch)
        default      599.000px = 59.90ch   MEET
        user-opened  378.958px = 37.90ch   FAIL
        LOST ON ONE CLICK: 220.042px = 22.00ch.

D108, BOTH HALVES — keep them together, because each half without the other misleads:
  - "0 of 9 user-opened cells MEET" was CORRECT for the three widths D108 measured, and it still
    reproduces on 65541e2d4: at 1024, 900 and 800 x three faces, 9 of 9 FAIL. Deleting it would erase
    a true finding. Repeating it WITHOUT its three-width scope would imply it covers the desktop set,
    which it does not — at 1440 and 1280 five of six cells MEET.
  - Its companion claim "9 of 9 default cells MEET" is now FALSE. Forced Georgia FAILS in the DEFAULT
    state at 1024 (54.22ch), and also at 1280 (53.95ch) and 700 (51.33ch). Do not repeat it.

Restated for the sub-wide band only: 0 of the 15 desktop cells at 1024 through 700 MEET 55ch in the user-opened state — not one width, not one face. (Earlier revisions said "0 of 18", counting 1024/900/800/764/700/640 x three faces; viewport 640 is NOT a D107 desktop row, so the desktop-scoped count is 15 of 15, and 640 fails too but is a separately-owned shortfall, section 5.)

THE SCRIM, reported and NEVER folded into the headline (D111). All 21 sub-wide user-opened rows carry dimmed_content_px at scrim_alpha 0.55. The scrim (.editor-with-preview:has(.bp-doc-sidebar.is-open)::after, position absolute, inset 0, pointer-events none) DIMS at 55% black; it does not hide, so it is reported alongside and never subtracted. Counting it as occlusion would make visible = 0px at every sub-wide user-opened width, after which no seal is ever possible and the metric can no longer rank improvement. Counting it as nothing is the older defect D36 named. Silence about it is what is forbidden; neither arithmetic alone is.

RECORD-KEEPING FLAG the successor should close in one line, filed as spd-b44-dimmed-vs-visible-label-identity: wave 7 pasted the numbers 378.958 / 446.875 / 396.875 / 394.844 / 331.115 / 270.967 as dimmed_content_px per width, and wave 8 carries the SAME numbers as visible_content_px. Both readings are coherent — D111 records scrim_covers_content_fully:true, so every pixel the reader can geometrically see is also dimmed and the two quantities coincide — but the identity is INFERRED here, not read off a committed artifact, because no run JSON exists anywhere in the repo (D131). Confirm it against one row of raw output before quoting either label as the other.

THE DEFINITIONAL ARTEFACT, named plainly because it is the metric WORKING and not failing (D109): at viewport 1024 the LAYOUT number IMPROVES on opening, 599px -> 640px, because the 41px in-flow strip leaves flow and hands its width back to the panel — while the VISIBLE number COLLAPSES to 378.958px, because the inspector becomes a 300px absolute overlay. On the single interaction this epic is about, the layout metric and the reader move in OPPOSITE directions. That is the strongest available argument for an occlusion-derived metric: it needs no counterfactual and it is on the deployed build now.

The crush is RECOVERABLE — a second click returns the panel to is-collapsed and the column recovers to 599px at viewport 1024. That mitigates severity; it does not answer the question.

=====================================================================
2. THE IN-FLOW CEILING (charter D126) — this is what makes this task decidable
=====================================================================

FORMULA:  ceiling_px = min(panel_px, surface cap 720) - read gutter - (55 x that face's probe px/ch)

Read in words: the widest in-flow inspector that can coexist with a >=55ch reading column at that width and face. A shipped inspector WIDER than the ceiling cannot reach 55ch by any amount of docking.

viewport | min(panel,720) | gutter | native | Georgia | Source Serif 4
  1440   |      720       |   80   |  90.0  |   32.4  |   135.5
  1280   |      720       |   80   |  90.0  |   32.4  |   135.5
  1024   |      720       |   80   |  90.0  |   32.4  |   135.5
   900   |      720       |   80   |  90.0  |   32.4  |   135.5
   800   |      720       |   80   |  90.0  |   32.4  |   135.5
   764   |      720       |   48   | 122.0  |   64.4  |   167.5
   700   |      656       |   48   |  58.0  |    0.4  |   103.5
   640   |      596       |   48   |  -2.0  |  -59.6  |    43.5

The ceiling is FLAT at 90.0 / 32.4 / 135.5 from 800 all the way through 1440, because .bp-paper-surface's own max-width:720px binds at every one of those widths. WIDENING THE VIEWPORT BUYS NO INSPECTOR ROOM. That is the single most important line in this section: the successor cannot solve this by assuming bigger screens.

At 640 the ceiling is NEGATIVE on two faces — even an inspector of ZERO width leaves native 54.80ch, 0.20ch short. Nothing about the inspector can fix viewport 640; it is a gutter-and-type-scale problem, and the epic names it as an owned shortfall rather than chasing it (D100 as amended by D106).

VALIDATED, NOT ASSERTED. The model reproduces four independent charter figures it was not fitted to:
  - 1024, all three faces -> 90.0 / 32.4 / 135.5, matching D126 exactly.
  - 700 forced Georgia -> 0.42px, matching D126's 0.4px.
  - 640 native minus spd-b29's shipped 41px strip -> 548 - 41 = 507px = 50.70ch, matching D106's measured 507px and its "4.30ch short" to the pixel.
  - 640 native with a zero-width strip -> 548px = 54.80ch = 0.20ch short, matching D100's original ~0.2ch native figure.
It also reproduces D104's default content_px to the pixel at 900 / 800 / 764 / 640.

WHAT IS SHIPPED TODAY, measured against its own ceiling:
  - The default state ships a 41px in-flow strip. At 1024 that is 8.6px OVER the forced-Georgia ceiling of 32.4px — which is why viewport 1024 / Georgia reads 54.22ch FAIL in the DEFAULT state.

    OWNERSHIP OF THAT SHORTFALL, stated because it has been misattributed (wave-9 D141). The forced-Georgia
    DEFAULT failures at 1280 (53.95ch) and 1024 (54.22ch) are owned by
    spd-b42-georgia-default-shortfall-inflow-width. They are NOT owned by
    spd-b28-floor-binds-georgia-1280-overflow, whose slug asserts two mechanisms and NEITHER IS PRESENT on
    65541e2d4: the artifact's own bind test — measure, force min-inline-size to 0px inline, re-measure,
    restore, where a width change IS the bind — reports floor.binds FALSE in 0 OF 54 ROWS, and
    overflow.overflow_px is 0 with horizontal_scroll false in exactly those cells. THE FLOOR NEVER BINDS
    AND NOTHING OVERFLOWS. The actual cause is arithmetic and dull: the .bp-paper-surface 720px cap minus
    the 80px read gutter leaves 640px, and Georgia's 11.0469 px/ch advance turns 640px into 57.93ch at
    the widths where the cap binds cleanly — but at 1280 and 1024 the panel is narrower than 720px, the
    cap does not bind, and the remainder lands just under 55ch. Attribute it to spd-b42, by full slug.
  - The user-opened state ships a 300px absolute overlay. At 1024 that is 3.3x the native ceiling and 9.3x the Georgia ceiling.

=====================================================================
DOCKING IS ARITHMETICALLY DEAD AT 1024 — with a correction to the figure
=====================================================================

Dock the shipped 300px inspector in flow at viewport 1024:
  panel 720px - dock 300px = 420px of panel left for the surface.
  The 720px surface cap no longer binds (420 < 720), so the read gutter comes off:
  420px - 80px gutter = 340px of CONTENT = 34.00ch native / 30.78ch Georgia / 37.07ch Source Serif 4.

Against today's overlay at 378.958px = 37.90ch native, docking the same 300px inspector LOSES the reader 38.958px on every face. Docking is worse than the overlay it would replace, and it is nowhere near 55ch.

CORRECTION ON THE RECORD (do not propagate the older figure). The wave-8 slice brief and the Decide narration both state this as "a 300px dock at 1024 leaves 420px (~42ch), WORSE than the overlay it would replace". The CONCLUSION is correct and survives; the FIGURE quoted for it does not. 420px is the panel remainder BEFORE the 80px gutter, not content, and 420px is LARGER than the overlay's 378.958px — so as quoted the number refutes the sentence it was supporting. The gutter-subtracted 340px / 34.00ch is the correct comparable and it is genuinely worse by 38.958px. Recorded here in full rather than silently swapped, per this epic's own standard that a claim and its arithmetic must agree.

THE HONEST COUNTERWEIGHT the successor must weigh, not skip: a docked 340px column is UNDIMMED, whereas today's overlay 378.958px is dimmed at scrim_alpha 0.55 across its whole area. Comparing 340px of clean text against 378.958px of 55%-dimmed text is not a pure pixel comparison, and D111 forbids folding the scrim into the headline in EITHER direction. State how you are weighing it before you weigh it.

NOT VERIFIED, and stated as such: every ch figure and every ceiling here is a macOS reading with scrollbar_width_px 0 (overlay scrollbars). A classic ~15px scrollbar pushes the borderline rows further down. The whole table is a BEST CASE, on TWO independent axes — the scrollbar (filed as spd-b43-measure-scrollbar-platform-optimism) and the resolution of the unforced serif stack (section 2a, filed as spd-palatino-linotype-unmeasured). Neither is left implicit, and neither has been measured.

=====================================================================
2a. "NATIVE" IS A PLATFORM VARIABLE, NOT A FACE (wave-9 D145)
=====================================================================

The tables above have a native column. There is no such font. "native" is whatever the UNFORCED serif
stack resolves to on the machine the instrument ran on, and that machine was a Mac. THE NATIVE ROW IS A
macOS READING, and on other platforms the same stack resolves to different metrics and different verdicts.
This is inheritable and unresolved.

  macOS   -> IOWAN OLD STYLE. Advance 1139/2048 em; at font-size 18px that is
             18 x 1139/2048 = 10.0107421875px, which Chrome's LayoutUnit quantises to 1/64px:
             floor(10.0107421875 x 64)/64 = 640/64 = EXACTLY 10.0000px. The clean 10.0000 px/ch probe
             in every native row is therefore GENUINE — it is Iowan measured and floored, NOT a
             suspiciously-round fallback value, and not the instrument rounding. Verified by deriving
             it from the font's own em metrics rather than by trusting the probe.
  Linux (stock)         -> no Iowan, no Palatino; the stack falls through to the SOURCE SERIF 4 WEBFONT
                           at 9.1719 px/ch, which MEETS at every desktop width in the default state.
                           Stock Linux is the best case and is not at risk.
  Linux (msttcorefonts) -> resolves the UNFORCED stack to GEORGIA. This is the one that matters: such a
                           user is not running a forced-face test, they are LIVING the three inherited
                           failing cells for real, at 1280, 1024 and 700, with no override applied.
                           Georgia is not a synthetic stress face; it is a reachable default.
  Windows -> PALATINO LINOTYPE, second in the stack and the Windows-native winner. IT HAS NEVER BEEN
             MEASURED, by this epic or any other.

THE PALATINO PASS/FAIL CONDITION, pre-computed so whoever measures it does not have to re-derive it.
The tightest DEFAULT desktop cell is viewport 700, where visible_content_px is 567.000. A face MEETS 55ch
there iff its advance is at most 567/55 = 10.30909px, which at 18px is 0.57273 em. So:

    PALATINO LINOTYPE FAILS iff its 0 advance exceeds 0.5727 em.

That threshold sits BETWEEN the two faces already measured — Iowan at 0.5556 em (passes, 56.70ch) and
Georgia at 0.6137 em (fails, 51.33ch) — which is exactly why the answer cannot be guessed from the
existing table in either direction. Filed as spd-palatino-linotype-unmeasured; measure it before any
ruling claims platform coverage.

THE GENERAL POINT for the successor: a per-face verdict is only as portable as the stack that produces
the face. Any ruling that suspends or upholds the 55ch bar should say WHICH PLATFORM'S native column it
is ruling on, or say that it rules on the forced faces only and treats native as advisory.

=====================================================================
3. THE PRE-REGISTERED QUESTION (charter D127) — OPEN and UNDECIDED
=====================================================================

Because no shape at viewport 1024 satisfies both a usable inspector and a >=55ch column — the ceiling is 32.4px under forced Georgia and the narrowest useful inspector is many times that — the resolution is necessarily a RULING about what the bar MEANS in that mode. Rulings belong in a charter, not in CSS.

THE SUCCESSOR QUESTION IS THEREFORE NOT "DOCK OR OVERLAY". Docking is dead by arithmetic, above. The question is:

    IS A USER-SUMMONED INSPECTOR A MODE IN WHICH THE >=55ch BAR IS SUSPENDED?

Registered here as the OPENING POSITION, PRE-REGISTERED and UNDECIDED.

WHY THIS EPIC DECLINED TO RULE IT EXEMPT. Exempting a mode AFTER seeing an unfavourable table is D107's gerrymandering with extra steps. D107 fixed the definition of "desktop rows" before any table was consulted precisely so the epic could not pick its own passing grade; granting this mode an exemption at the moment its table came back 0-for-18 would have spent that discipline on the first inconvenient result. The refusal is not a verdict that the mode ISN'T exempt — it is a refusal to decide it in the wrong order.

THE SUCCESSOR MAY RULE IT EXEMPT. The binding condition: STATE THE RULE BEFORE YOU LOOK AT YOUR OWN TABLE. Write the exemption, its scope and its limits into the charter as a decision; then measure. A rule written after the measurement is not a rule, it is a rationalisation.

WHAT A PASSING OUTCOME LOOKS LIKE — either of these two, nothing else:
  (a) A shape ships and MEASURES >=55ch at the D107 desktop rows (1440, 1280, 1024, 900, 800, 764, 700) in the user-opened state, on the deployed build, per face, with every remaining shortfall NAMED and OWNED; or
  (b) A pre-registered ruling suspends the bar for the user-summoned mode, states its scope and limits BEFORE the table is consulted, and the resulting state is measured and recorded anyway.
Both paths require a run against the deployed build. Neither is satisfiable by argument.

WHAT DOES NOT COUNT: arriving at (b) by not measuring the state. That is exactly the failure D108 caught.

SHAPES STILL LIVE (docking is not among them):
  - A NARROWER inspector. Bounded by the ceiling: at 1024 you have 90.0px native and 32.4px Georgia to spend. Note that even 90px of in-flow inspector is not obviously useful, and 32.4px certainly is not.
  - A TAB-BAR DRILL (the Sanity pattern, section 4) — no overlay at narrow widths at all; the user drills and the column is never obstructed. This is the only live shape that satisfies the headline without any exemption.
  - PUSH-AND-SHRINK that accepts a sub-55ch column WHILE the user is deliberately reading metadata. This is shape (b) wearing CSS: it needs the ruling first.
  - Raising the .bp-paper-surface 720px cap, which is what makes the ceiling flat from 800 to 1440. UNEXAMINED by this epic and out of its fence — the cap is a measure-of-line-length decision owned elsewhere. If the successor wants inspector room at 1280+, this is the only lever that creates any, and it must be opened as a type-measure question rather than a layout hack.

=====================================================================
4. THE COMPARABLES, CORRECTED (charter D129) — one clean citation beats three shaky ones
=====================================================================

MATERIAL DESIGN 3 — CORRECTED, and D101's version must not be quoted again. D101 described a "permanent / persistent / temporary" taxonomy; that is MD2 ARCHIVED drawer language. Current MD3 is TWO-TIER: standard and modal. What MD3 actually states, and nothing beyond it:
  - Standard side sheets are "used mostly in medium to expanded window sizes" = 600-1199dp. NOT the "~1024-1440px" D101 attributed to it; MD3 does not state that range.
  - The ONLY explicit endorsement of a standard side sheet AS A THIRD PANE is scoped to EXTRA-LARGE, 1600dp and above — ABOVE every width this epic tests.
  - The expanded page (840-1199dp, which covers both 900 and 1024) mentions side sheets NOWHERE.
  - Modal is reserved for COMPACT, under 600dp.
  - A standard side sheet SHRINKS the body area rather than overlaying it.
  What MD3 genuinely supports here: overlaying at 1024 is the COMPACT-tier behaviour applied outside compact, and the sanctioned non-compact behaviour shrinks the column. It does NOT supply a third-pane endorsement at any width this epic tests. No claim in this task carries a pixel range MD3 does not state.

CONTENTFUL — STRUCK. Both first-party pages were fetched directly and via rendered DOM and contain NO layout-mechanism and NO responsive language at all. The "slide-out drawer" framing was unsourced search synthesis. It is removed from the comparison bar rather than downgraded, and it may not be re-cited without a first-party source.

SANITY STUDIO — RETAINED, width UNCONFIRMED. Panes collapse into a tab bar and the user drills; it does not overlay at narrow widths. The pattern stands as sourced; the exact breakpoints are not confirmed. This remains the single closest analogue to the headline, and the only sourced product that solves it by refusing to overlay.

LINEAR — CHECKED, FOUND, INCONCLUSIVE. /docs/peek exists, so D101's blanket "no public documentation" is WRONG for Linear specifically — but the page is silent on mechanism. Recorded as checked rather than as absent, so the next wave does not re-run the same search and reach the same dead end.

NOTION — first-party rationale, and it is this epic's own problem stated by someone else. Notion made its page-details panel default to the user's LAST state in Oct 2024, because an open panel by default "could distract from the main content and create navigation issues with multiple scrollbars."

STANDING LIMIT ON ALL OF THE ABOVE: no comparable was found that ships a document inspector OPEN BY DEFAULT AND OVERLAYING primary content at laptop widths. That is DIRECTIONAL support and is stated as directional. A wave claiming a live cross-product comparison must have driven the sessions.

=====================================================================
5. VIEWPORT 500 IS DATA, NOT A FAILING DESKTOP ROW
=====================================================================

Viewport 500 measures 174.944px user-opened (17.49ch native / 15.84ch Georgia / 19.07ch Source Serif 4) and it is carried as DATA ONLY. It is PHONE bucket, where the pane rail vanishes ENTIRELY — not the 44px strip narrow keeps — so the overlay maths differ in kind, not degree. The epic NEVER gated phone on >=55ch (D100): phone's criterion is navigability plus no horizontal scroll, both already met (D88/D56), and the vision frames phone as a single-pane drill. D107 excludes viewport 500 from the desktop rows BY NAME. Do not report it as a failing desktop row and do not extrapolate the sub-wide pattern onto it.

Viewport 640 is likewise excluded from the desktop rows as a NAMED, OWNED shortfall (D100 as amended by D106), and its ceiling is negative on two faces, so no inspector shape addresses it.
